column1: # alerts.tsv — the machine-readable half of decisions/alerts.md.
# The ruling is the source; this file is the same rows in the shape the program reads them in, and
# the seed in contract/schema.sql is the same rows again in the shape a cell holds them.
# acceptance/b03-observation.sh holds all three against each other on every run — a row in one and
# not in another is drift, and drift is an error rather than a silent omission (the rule OP-1 and
# `slot` is what SP-B03-3's "exactly four" is enforced with: one of four, unique, and present
# exactly when the alert wakes somebody. An alert with no slot is a display, and a display never
# wakes a human — which is the whole of the panel's closing sentence.
# `signal` names where the state comes from. `node.ping` and `node.disk` are properties of a
# machine and not of the state database: an evaluation that has no node in front of it says it
# cannot answer rather than reporting a green it did not measure (Q-02).

column5: 3 failed pings in a row at the heartbeat interval (OP-4: 15 s)
20 samples 1 minute apart, none below its predecessor, the last above the first
the last hour >= 3x the mean of the 6 hours before it, and >= 10 rejections in absolute terms
a daily pot at >= 90 % of a cap while less than 75 % of its day has passed
the work disk at >= 85 % full (SP-A05-5: the first consumable with an alert)
refused targets per project and target, so a cluster is visible (SP-B02-5)
